verdict.rationale: Gmail supports rule-based automation via Filters that automatically trigger actions (label, forward, delete) whenever mail matching criteria arrives, and the Gmail API offers push notifications so developers can build custom background automations reacting to mailbox changes. However, these are either simple non-AI rule engines or require external developer-built infrastructure — there's no first-party AI-native/agentic automation builder for end users; Gemini in Gmail features (summarize, draft, organize) are on-demand assistant actions, not autonomous background agents. missing for 10: end-user-facing AI-driven automation/agent builder, evidence of autonomous multi-step agentic workflows, first-party 'set it and forget it' AI automation UI.
